title: Constructibility of the degree-zero open direct image
statement:
Let $X$ be of finite type over a field, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an
open immersion,
and let $F$ be a
constructible
module sheaf over a finite commutative ring on $U_{\Et}$.
Then $j_*F$ is
constructible on $X_{\Et}$.

proof.text: Finite type over a field makes X Noetherian, and the open subscheme U is Noetherian. Compare the finite-constant-value constructibility predicate with IsConstructibleSheaf. For each x in U, give its closure Z the reduced induced structure. Z is integral: its underlying space is the irreducible closure of a point and the subscheme is reduced. Pull back F to Z, take a dense lisse open D, and shrink D to a nonempty normal open V. The point over x is generic in Z, so it belongs to every nonempty open, in particular V.

Let h:V -> U and a=jh. Put L=h^*F, which is finite locally constant by pullback composition. The quasi-compact immersion a factors as an open immersion into its scheme-theoretic image Y followed by a closed immersion into X. Y is integral: the map V -> Y is dense and scheme-theoretically dominant, so its image is irreducible and Y is reduced. Y is of finite type over the same field. Apply the normal-open direct-image theorem to V -> Y, then closed-immersion constructibility to Y -> X. Composition of direct images identifies the result with j_*h_*L.

The geometric point over x lifts along h because h is an immersion and its image contains x. The unit F -> h_*h^*F is monomorphic on this geometric stalk: under the inverse-image/stalk composition isomorphism, composing the stalk map of the unit with the stalk map of the counit is the identity, by the adjunction triangle identity. Thus for every point there is a map out of F injective on its stalk whose direct image under j is constructible.

Apply Noetherian finite selection to this family of unit maps, indexed by points of U. It gives a finite subset S such that F -> product_{x in S} G_x is mono. Each j_*G_x is constructible, so their finite product is constructible by finite biproducts and the Serre closure properties. The functor j_* preserves monomorphisms and finite products, hence gives an injection j_*F -> product_{x in S} j_*G_x. Constructibility of subsheaves on Noetherian X gives constructibility of j_*F. Convert back to the original finite-constant-value predicate.

proof_origin.place: Normal-lisse-open and closed-image construction of paragraph 2, applied to point closures; finite selection of stalk-injective adjunction units replaces the supported-kernel induction of paragraphs 1, 3 and 4.

tool_uses.why: Steps 6 and 7 need closure of constructible sheaves under subsheaves; this imported theorem is from the generic constructible-sheaf unit and no node in sk-prop-a1-kummer supplies that closure.
The generic reduction morphism is a universal homeomorphism; this fact is not supplied by the affine-line unit and is needed before applying universal-homeomorphism invariance.
The construction $L=h^*F$ uses the generic inverse-image definition; the affine-line unit has no local definition of sheaf inverse image.
Reduction needs reflection of module-sheaf constructibility under a surjective qcqs morphism; this generic descent criterion is not a replacement for any affine-line-unit argument.
The kernel restriction and constant-coefficient identifications use this generic exact inverse-image theorem; the unit has no such theorem.
Only the underived identity h^{-1}h_*=id is used to show the kernel vanishes on V; this is a generic open-immersion fact, not the Kunneth route.
The closed adjunction unit is checked on stalks using the generic inverse-image stalk isomorphism with its stated germ compatibility; no node of this unit supplies that compatibility.
The nondense induction case needs the generic construction and affine ideal description of the reduced closure, not another proof route.
The nondense induction case needs the generic reduced-source factorization theorem to obtain the morphism to the reduced closure.
The proof uses the generic Noetherian-induction principle; the affine-line unit supplies no separate version.
